WRITING SUB-TEST – TEST BOOKLET




INSTRUCTIONS TO CANDIDATES
You must write your answer for the Writing sub-test in the Writing Answer Booklet.

You must NOT remove OET material from the test room.
  Occupational English Test

 WRITING SUB-TEST:         MEDICINE
 TIME ALLOWED:             READING TIME: 5 MINUTES
                           WRITING TIME: 40 MINUTES

 Read the case notes and complete the writing task which follows.

  Notes:

 You are a GP in a city clinic. Mr David Taylor is a patient in your general practice.

 PATIENT DETAILS:
 Name:     Mr David Taylor
 DOB:      01/08/1965 ( age 55 )

 Patient history:
                  Occupation - Business traveller
                  Divorced - has 2 children
                  lives alone at home
                  Drinks alcohol 2 glasses/w
                  Non-smoker since 2010
                  No known allergies

Family history:    Father - died of Kidney failure
                  Mother - asthma
                  Brother - gout

Past medical history:

                  2000: gout - colchicine (Lengout), allopurinol, paracetamol.
                  2002: laryngitis.
                  2003: appendectomy.
                  2010: kidney stones.
                  01/06/2010: Severe gout attack - steroid injection, colchicine, allopurinol.
                  01/09/2010: Gout attack - Advise Pt re lifestyle changes to stop smoking,
                               reduce alcohol, decrease dietary red meat, drink more fluid.
                  05/12/2010: Pt appears well. Successful lifestyle adjustment.
                  2011: Depression ( ? due to gout ), flouxetine
                  2011-2020: No gout attacks.
 13/06/2020

   Subjective:     Complains of pain in RT big toe.
                   Swelling in RT foot, RT big toe.
                   Pain in Rt flank.
                   Red colour urine - frequency normal.

   Objective:      BP: 120/80, HR: 90, RR: 22, T 37.8
                   Pt anxious, shortness of breath.
                   Inflamed, red first RT toe.
                   Tophus - under RT big toe.
   Treatment       Colchicine (Lengout) 1 mg
                   NSAIDS

   Plan:           Refer to a Rheumatologist for urgent assessment.
                   Removal of tophus?.
                   Refer to a Urologist.




   Writing Task:


   Using the information given in the case notes, write a letter of referral to Dr Still, a
   Rheumatologist at City Hospital, for assessment of Mr Taylor. Address the letter to Dr
   Malcom Still, Rheumatologist, City Hospital, Suite 32, 55 Main Road, Newtown.
   In your answer:
       ●
        ●




             Expand the relevant notes into complete sentences
        ●




       ●     Do not use note form
        ●




       ●     Use letter format

   The body of the letter should be approximately 180–200 words.
 Any answers recorded here will not be marked.




                                                N K
                                      L A
                          B
